2027-01-19.title: Tuesday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul
The Lord will remember his covenant for ever
The sabbath was made for humankind
2027-01-19.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January).
2027-01-19.verse: We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain,
theo: Hebrews encourages a tired community: “God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints.” Do not become sluggish, but imitate those who “through faith and patience inherit the promises”, like Abraham. God bound himself by an oath, so that “we… might be strongly encouraged to seize the hope set before us. We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” Our anchor is not thrown into the shifting sand of this world; it is fixed in heaven, where Jesus has gone ahead of us.

In the Gospel the Pharisees object when the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath. Jesus recalls David eating the holy bread when he was hungry, and declares: “The sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.” God's laws are gifts for our life, not burdens to crush it. The Lord's Day is his gift of rest and worship, and Christ himself is its Lord.
outline: Ask: what keeps a ship steady in a storm?
Fixed in heaven where Jesus has gone.
“A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
live: Return to one good work you have grown tired of.
Plan this Sunday as a day of worship, family and rest.
2027-01-19.prayer: Faithful God, you never forget our love and you have given us hope as an anchor for the soul. Keep us patient in faith, and teach us to keep your day as a gift of life, with Christ the Lord of the sabbath. Amen.
altar: Hebrews says our hope enters “behind the curtain”, where Jesus our High Priest has gone. At Mass heaven's sanctuary touches earth.

quick: God does not forget the love we show.
Hope is a sure anchor fixed in heaven.
The sabbath was made for humankind.
2027-01-19.action: Plan this Sunday as a day of worship, family and rest.
2027-01-19.question: Where is the anchor of my soul fixed?

family.explain: An anchor keeps a boat from drifting away in the wind. Our hope in Jesus is like an anchor that keeps our hearts steady.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel hopeless.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family do to make Sunday special for God?”

illus: Fishermen in Neendakara say the anchor rope must be long and the anchor heavy; in a storm the boat swings but does not drift onto the rocks. A widow there said after a hard year: my boat swung a lot, but my anchor was in heaven. I did not drift.

pm.open: Faithful God, our hope is anchored in you. Steady our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: God will not overlook your work and love (Hebrews 6:10). What good work have I grown tired of?
A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul (Hebrews 6:19). What steadies me in storms?
The sabbath was made for humankind (Mark 2:27). How do I keep the Lord's Day?
interc: For those who serve the poor and feel tired.
For those who have lost hope.
For a renewed love of Sunday worship in our families.
For our group, that we may persevere in faith and patience.
pm.close: Father, you have given us hope as an anchor. Keep us steady in faith and joyful in your day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews speaks to tired Christians: God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints (Hebrews 6:10). No act of love is forgotten.
Do not become sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises, like Abraham. God bound himself by an oath so that we might seize the hope set before us.
We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain (Hebrews 6:19). Our anchor is fixed in heaven, where Jesus has gone ahead of us.

In the Gospel Jesus says: the sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath (Mark 2:27–28). God's law serves our life. Let us keep the Lord's Day as a gift, and hold fast to our anchor of hope. Amen.
kids: Children, an anchor keeps a boat from floating away. Hope in Jesus keeps our hearts safe. Hold on to Jesus!

intro: Theme: “A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
Persevering love, hope anchored in heaven, the Lord of the sabbath.

q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain,
points.apply: Hold on to one promise of God in a present trouble.

q: He has gained renown by his wonderful deeds; the LORD is gracious and merciful.
For God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints, as you still do.
points.apply: Return to one good work you abandoned.

q: Remember the sabbath day, and keep it holy.
Then he said to them, “The sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.”
points.apply: Make Sunday a day of worship, family and rest.

concl: God remembers our love and anchors our hope.
Christ is Lord of our time and our rest.
2027-01-19.resolve: Keep next Sunday holy as a family.
